method.label: Method
method.title: How I work
method.lead: The same process for an app, a platform or an internal tool: five phases, each closed by a result you can check.

phases.name: Understand
phases.title: The problem before the code.
phases.body: I start from the people who will use the software and what has to change in their work. The outcome is prioritised requirements, testable acceptance criteria and the risks to settle early.

phases.name: Design
phases.title: Decisions written down, not remembered.
phases.body: I shape the architecture around real needs, not trends. Every significant choice goes into a short record with context, alternatives and consequences, so whoever comes next knows why things are the way they are.
practices: Data and permissions designed from the start

phases.name: Build
phases.title: Small steps, always verified.
phases.body: I work in short increments on separate branches. Every change goes through review and automated tests before it reaches the main branch, and the version number follows the kind of change.

phases.name: Release
phases.title: Boring releases, on purpose.
phases.body: The pipeline checks, builds and publishes with no manual steps. New versions reach a share of users first; if errors rise, the release rolls itself back.

phases.name: Operate
phases.title: The work goes on after release.
phases.body: I measure response times and errors against agreed objectives and get an alert before a problem reaches users. Documentation and handover are part of the delivery.

method.principlesTitle: Principles that hold in every phase

principles.title: Security from the start
principles.body: Secrets out of the code, least privilege, dependencies kept current and checked.

principles.title: Justified simplicity
principles.body: The simplest solution that meets the requirements. Extra complexity is argued in writing.

principles.title: Measured performance
principles.body: Load and response times with a budget and real numbers, not impressions.

principles.title: Accessibility built in
principles.body: Contrast, keyboard and screen readers checked during development, not at the end.

principles.title: Regular communication
principles.body: Updates on a fixed rhythm, problems raised as soon as they appear, decisions shared.

principles.title: Code that lasts
principles.body: Clear names, shared conventions, no part that only one person can maintain.
